source_policy: Primary and normative sources define their own surfaces only. This map paraphrases bounded rules and stores links; it does not reproduce or silently generalize protected documentation.

bounded_findings: The pipeline has explicit contracts for pivots, triangulation, multiple UV sets, smoothing, vertex colors, custom collision, sockets, materials, and LODs.
Manual triangulation gives the author control over the final triangle result; automatic triangulation can alter it.
Custom collision and sockets depend on target naming and export rules.
A material or texture import still requires target-side inspection because not every map is automatically connected.
FBX version compatibility is target-engine specific and must be recorded.
nonclaims: Unreal-specific names and FBX rules are not universal interchange rules.
Successful import does not prove visual quality, performance, collision fitness, or gameplay readiness.

bounded_findings: Geometry and material counts trade visual fidelity against rendering and animation cost; the correct balance depends on target platform, scene complexity, and required appearance.
Runtime vertex counts may exceed DCC geometric vertex counts because normals, UVs, or vertex colors can split vertices.
Animated assets add bone, skinning, and renderer costs that cannot be inferred from polygon count alone.
nonclaims: The documentation does not supply a universal polygon or material budget for every project.
A low authored vertex count does not by itself prove low runtime cost.

bounded_findings: Mesh LOD reduces distant rendering work by switching among decreasing-detail meshes.
LOD assets are a system of geometry and transition behavior, not one isolated reduced mesh.
nonclaims: Triangle reduction does not prove acceptable silhouette, shading, material continuity, or transition quality.

bounded_findings: Lightmap UVs may be authored or generated and occupy target-defined UV channels.
Texture UV success does not imply valid lightmap UVs; target use and channels must be explicit.
nonclaims: Automatic lightmap UV generation does not prove artifact-free baked lighting in the target scene.

bounded_findings: glTF declares a right-handed coordinate system, meter units, and explicit transformation rules.
Its core physically based material model is metallic-roughness with defined base-color, metallic, roughness, normal, occlusion, emissive, and alpha semantics.
Meshes, morph targets, skins, joint hierarchies, animation channels, samplers, and interpolation have explicit structural contracts.
Color and data textures have different transfer-function requirements; channel meaning must be preserved.
nonclaims: glTF conformance does not prove target-engine feature parity, aesthetic fidelity, memory cost, or gameplay fitness.
A renderer may extend or translate the core material model; those differences require target evidence.

bounded_findings: A declared validator can provide repeatable structural conformance evidence for the exact asset and validator version.
nonclaims: Validator success is not visual, performance, animation, collision, gameplay, art-direction, or legal acceptance.

derived_professional_rules.rule: Derive budgets from the named project, platform, scene, camera/use context, and measurement plan; never encode universal triangle, texture, material, bone, collision, or LOD counts.
Lock or explicitly record final topology, triangulation, UV seams, normals, tangents, and target bake assumptions before accepting tangent-space detail; rebake after changes that invalidate them.
Record material model, texture color/data spaces, channel meanings, alpha mode, target shader mapping, and renderer-specific differences.
Each LOD requires both budget measurement and target-context visual transition evidence; neither substitutes for the other.
Treat structural validation, target import, target visual observation, measured performance, and play-context verification as separate gates tied to one exact candidate.

research_gaps: Representative asset-class production studies and human expert review.
Character skinning and deformation, foliage, vehicles, weapons, photogrammetry, cloth, destruction, procedural assets, and virtualized-geometry pipelines.
Current DCC-specific authoring and bake procedures for each adopted toolchain.
Browser/WebGL/WebGPU delivery budgets, mesh or texture compression extensions, and target-device evidence.
Cross-engine material translation and tangent-basis compatibility fixtures.
